blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the senior level, the British relationship with time is not merely about punctuality — it is about the cultural perception of professionalism itself. A leader who consistently runs meetings over, arrives late, or demands answers within minutes is sending a message whether they intend to or not: 'my time is more important than yours'. In British executive culture, that message is rarely forgiven. It may not be corrected out loud. It may even be rewarded in the short term, because the person looks 'driven'.

But over a few quarters, the best people in the organisation quietly arrange not to work with them. When something hard needs to be delivered, the team that could have made it succeed is somehow unavailable. The damage is real, yet almost invisible, because nobody names it.

The senior leaders who last in British organisations are almost always the ones who treat other people's time as scarce and valuable, even when their own is under pressure. If one had to pick a single habit that predicts executive longevity, it would be this: finish meetings a minute or two early, consistently, over years. That one habit is worth more than almost any strategy.

items.q: According to the text, at senior level the British relationship with time is primarily about…
options: the length of the working day
items.why: "it is about the cultural perception of professionalism itself" — pontualidade é só a superfície.

items.q: Why might a chronically late leader be rewarded in the short term?
options: Because British culture values speed above all
items.why: "It may even be rewarded in the short term, because the person looks 'driven'."

items.q: The phrase "the team that could have made it succeed is somehow unavailable" most strongly suggests that…
options: the project was cancelled from above
the best people have quietly withdrawn their commitment
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que os melhores 'quietly arrange not to work with them' — a indisponibilidade é uma retirada silenciosa, não um acaso.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The cost of lateness can be almost invisible.
Small habits can outweigh strategy over time.
How a leader treats time signals how they value people.
Being visibly 'driven' is a reliable measure of leadership.
items.why: Inferência: o autor trata o 'driven' de curto prazo como uma armadilha que erode a equipe — não como medida confiável de liderança.

items.q: What does the author imply by calling the damage "real, yet almost invisible"?
options: The harm accumulates unnoticed because no one names it
The harm only appears in financial reports
The harm is minor and easily reversed
The harm is exaggerated by rivals
items.why: Inferência: 'because nobody names it' — o prejuízo se acumula sem ser dito em voz alta, por isso passa despercebido.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry dando forma a um 360 review de um executivo sênior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I've been sitting with this 360 for two days, because on paper the man is exceptional. His strategic thinking is the best on the board, and nobody disputes that. If the review were only about ideas, I'd have signed it off on Monday.

The problem is time. He runs every meeting fifteen minutes over, he replies to his own people at midnight and expects an answer by seven, and he is late — reliably, quietly late. Two years ago I'd have called that a scheduling issue. I no longer believe that. Had he protected other people's time the way he protects his own calendar, he would still have Priya and he would still have Daniel. Both of them asked to move teams, and neither of them said why. They didn't have to.

So I'm going to write the truth, carefully. Not that he's unprofessional — he isn't. But that his best people have started to treat him as expensive to work with, and the organisation is paying for it in a currency that never shows up in a quarterly number. If he'd finished one meeting early, just once, someone might have stayed.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why has Harry been hesitating over the review for two days?
options: The executive is about to be promoted
The board has told him what to write
The executive's strategic thinking is exceptional
He lacks any evidence of a problem
items.why: "on paper the man is exceptional… his strategic thinking is the best on the board" — o talento é o que torna o review difícil.

items.q: Which time behaviours does Harry describe?
options: He delegates all scheduling to Priya
He cancels meetings and ignores emails
He arrives early but leaves early too
He runs meetings over, emails at midnight, and is reliably late
items.why: "He runs every meeting fifteen minutes over, he replies… at midnight… and he is late — reliably, quietly late."

items.q: What does Harry imply about why Priya and Daniel asked to move teams?
options: They left because of how he treated their time, though they never said so
They disagreed with the company's strategy
They were reassigned by the board
items.why: Inferência: 'neither of them said why. They didn't have to' — Harry liga a saída ao desrespeito ao tempo, mesmo sem que digam.

items.q: When Harry says the cost shows up "in a currency that never shows up in a quarterly number", he means…
options: the problem will surface only next quarter
the damage is talent and trust, not a line on a financial report
the company undercharges for its services
the loss is measured in foreign exchange
items.why: Inferência: a 'moeda' invisível é a perda de pessoas e confiança — algo que não aparece no número trimestral.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's stance towards the executive?
options: Hostile and eager to see him removed
Uncertain whether any problem exists at all
Indifferent, treating it as routine paperwork
Fair but candid — respectful of the talent, honest about the cost
items.why: Inferência: ele reconhece o talento ('the man is exceptional') mas decide 'write the truth, carefully' — equilíbrio entre justiça e franqueza.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "His longevity at the top surprised those who expected him to burn out." Longevity here means…
options: how long he lasts in the role
items.why: Longevity = longevidade: por quanto tempo alguém se mantém no papel.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Even when he was under real pressure, he treated his colleagues' time as ___ — never something to be spent carelessly."
items.why: Scarce = escasso; tratar o tempo como escasso é respeitá-lo como recurso valioso.

items.q: "The habit was rewarded in the short term but punished over years." Rewarded means it was…
items.why: Rewarded = recompensado: recebeu reconhecimento ou benefício — ainda que só no curto prazo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When the hard project finally launched, the very people who could have carried it were ___."
items.why: Unavailable = indisponível: os melhores já haviam se afastado, ficando fora de alcance.

items.q: "He apologised, but the pattern was too consistent to be an accident." Consistent here means…
items.why: Consistently/consistent = de forma consistente: um padrão que se repete de modo confiável, não um deslize isolado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em avaliações e conversas de liderança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The chair still has to sign off on the final 360 review." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two of his best people quietly opted out of his projects." They…
items.why: Opt out of = optar por não participar; a retirada silenciosa dos melhores colaboradores.

items.q: "He never followed through on his promise to end meetings on time." He…
options: failed to carry the commitment to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; ele não cumpriu.

items.q: "Ending a meeting five minutes early does more to move the needle on trust than any speech." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Reading the review, the board began to join the dots between his lateness and the resignations." To join the dots means to…
options: connect separate facts into a clear pattern
items.why: Join the dots = ligar os pontos: perceber a conexão entre fatos antes vistos como isolados.
